newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Stet approves Seat unit spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Stet approves Seat unit spin-off.

text.p: An extraordinary shareholders meeting of Italian state telecoms holding Stet formally approved plans to spin off its telephone directory publishing unit Seat.
The meeting also nominated a five-member board for Seat which is due to be sold off by the end of the year, ahead of Stet's privatisation slated to take place by end-March 1997.
Following the split, state holding company IRI, which controls Stet, will hold some 60 percent of Seat with the remainder floated on the stock market.
Seat as a public company will have capital of 264 billion lire and net assets of 560.4 billion lire.
Stet managing director Ernesto Pascale told shareholders the procedure for a bourse quotation for Seat would be started immediately.
As to the value of Seat, which analysts believe could be worth over $2 billion, Pascale said "the Bourse Council should give an initial evaluation in the coming days."
IRI has already received 26 valid offers for Seat from both Italian and foreign companies.
On Friday, Italian telecoms operator Telecom Italia said it was ready to buy up to 20 percent of the ordinary shares in Seat after its sale.
